source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check OS boot without bitlocker
Disable or remove TPM device.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: The OS cannot boot directally. It shows the bitlocker recovery menu.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: Operator disables/removes TPM and observes the Windows BitLocker recovery menu; not remotely runnable.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO; correctly identifies the BIOS/TPM and recovery-screen boundary but repeats physical removal as though equivalent to disablement.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED; restricts the stimulus to an approved reversible BIOS disable and adds volume, recovery-key, KVM/OOB and restoration controls.
historical_reviews.round_02: No separate exact-code round-02 entry was found.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms physical TPM removal or clear is not an acceptable default interpretation.

original_test_intent: With an approved BitLocker-protected Windows boot volume, make the TPM unavailable through the owner-defined reversible mechanism and verify by direct boot-screen observation that Windows does not boot normally and instead requests BitLocker recovery, then restore the security state.
original_method: A qualified operator verifies the exact volume/protector and recovery key, records the baseline, disables TPM using the approved reversible BIOS setting unless the owner explicitly requires a different fixture method, reboots under KVM, captures the BitLocker recovery screen, restores TPM and proves normal boot and protector health.
manual_activity: The core stimulus and acceptance require a qualified operator to change TPM availability in BIOS or the approved hardware method and visually observe the pre-OS BitLocker recovery screen. The agent may prepare checks and analyze screenshots/logs but must not claim the manipulation or observation.
required_inputs: Exact Windows boot volume, BitLocker protector and current protection status
Verified recovery key and protected backup
Owner-approved reversible TPM disable method and explicit ruling on whether physical removal is in scope
BIOS/KVM/OOB access, qualified operator and maintenance/reboot approval
Restoration sequence and expected normal/recovery boot behavior
safety_requirements: Do not physically remove, clear or re-own TPM unless that exact operation is explicitly defined and separately approved; prefer the reversible BIOS setting.
Do not start without the verified recovery key and exact protected-volume identity.
Stop on unexpected boot, recovery-key, TPM, secure-boot or OOB failure and preserve the screen/log state.
Do not auto-retry reboots or improvise TPM/security changes; restore only through the approved sequence.
agent_execution_scope: Validate volume/protector/recovery, chosen TPM-unavailable method and restoration plan before the operator session.
Collect timestamped operator-attributed BIOS/KVM, recovery-screen, BMC/SEL and restored-boot evidence.
Compare observed behavior with the clarified expectation and report Tool Result without declaring PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Resolve the contradictory 'without bitlocker' heading and choose disable versus remove semantics.
Perform and attest the TPM availability change and boot-screen observation.
Restore the platform security state, review evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: There is no safe agent command for the specified BIOS/physical stimulus or pre-OS screen. DeepSeek's manual boundary is correct, but 'removed from boot' must not be interpreted as physical removal without an explicit decision.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the operator-run reversible BIOS/KVM method after exact owner definition; use read-only BitLocker status exports only as supporting pre/post evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TPM-unavailable stimulus, boot observation, recovery-menu criterion and 2/5-minute fields are preserved; disable and physical removal are not silently treated as equivalent.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a controlled operator procedure with verified recovery key, explicit BIOS setting, KVM video capture, one approved reboot, recovery-screen evidence and an atomic restoration/normal-boot check.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Windows, BIOS/TPM firmware, BitLocker policy and BMC/KVM versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project BitLocker/TPM recovery and platform BIOS documentation must define the reversible method.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Disambiguates disable versus remove and adds exact recovery/restoration evidence without changing the intended TPM-unavailable stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; recovery-screen behavior and restored normal boot are both required.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner decision on stimulus and recovery policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong volume/recovery data or physical TPM handling can cause lockout or hardware/security damage.

project_override_considerations: A project may select a reversible BIOS disable, supported fixture isolation or—only if explicitly required—physical removal. Evidence and claims must name the actual method; one method cannot be claimed as completion of another.
expected_evidence: Windows/volume/protector/TPM/secure-boot identity, verified recovery key and authorization
Baseline BitLocker/TPM status and exact chosen stimulus
Operator-attributed BIOS or hardware action plus timestamped KVM recovery-menu evidence
Restored TPM state, normal boot, Windows/security/BMC/SEL health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure heading says 'boot without bitlocker' while the criterion requires an active BitLocker recovery menu, and 'disable or remove TPM' presents materially different reversible and physical stimuli as interchangeable. The owner must define the intended condition and method.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The recovery-path intent is clear enough to review. The method ambiguity is recorded for owner resolution; the inherently human BIOS/physical and visual core is MANUAL ONLY rather than BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees that the agent cannot perform or observe the core, but tightens the unsafe physical-removal wording.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with MANUAL ONLY and retains its reversible disable, recovery-key, KVM and restoration gates.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records both semantic conflicts and requires claims to identify the actual stimulus used.

review_improvement: Prevents accidental TPM removal/clear and ensures recovery-screen evidence is tied to an exact BitLocker volume, key and reversible security-state change.
independent_technical_reasoning: Pre-OS TPM availability change and BitLocker screen observation are operator-owned core actions. The source's conflicting heading and non-equivalent stimulus choices cannot be normalized silently, but they do not obscure the overall recovery-response purpose.

source_provenance.primary: data/REVISED_commands_merged_with_raw.xlsx, Functionality row 232, read directly with openpyxl 3.1.5

no_automatic_retry: One approved reboot observation only. Preserve any unexpected recovery or boot state; do not cycle repeatedly, clear TPM or try alternate security changes automatically.
